name: read_int4
note: review: readInt4 mirrors :263-266, but ReadInt4Roundtrip states only the success path. The truncated-input ValueError (:266) is not stated, unlike in ReadUintExact and ReadFloat8Exact, so a read_int4 that pads or returns the short data passes.

name: read_stringnl
note: review: readRawnl, stripQuotes and escapeDecode mirror :344-362 for the default arguments (the decode=False/stripquotes=False uses are inlined into the callers), but ReadStringnlPlain assumes `0x5c ∉ body`, which removes the docstring's own promise that embedded escapes are undone (:339-341). No theorem states the 'no newline found' ValueError (:345-346), the quote-mismatch or no-quote errors (:352-358), or what escape_decode does, so a read_stringnl that ignores escapes, skips the newline check or skips the closing-quote check passes. name: read_string4

name: assure_pickle_consistency
note: review: The stated reason is wrong: it is not a test helper and is not 'called by no code'. :2290 calls it at import and :2291 deletes it, and it raises ValueError (failing the import) if the opcode table and pickle.py disagree. Re-note it as internal-bootstrap: called once at import (:2290), deleted (:2291), raises nothing on 3.15.2's consistent tables.

name: _genops
note: review: genopStep and genopsLoop mirror :2305-2326 (getpos, read(1), code2op lookup, the exhausted and unknown-opcode messages, reader, end position, the STOP break), and the opcode table is exact. But every theorem is vacuous on failure: GenopsFuelEnough, GenopsWellFormed (positions contiguous from 0, STOP last), DisFollowsGenops and OptimizeRawCopy all assume a successful parse or compare two runs, so a genopStep that always raises passes all four. Nothing states that genops accepts any stream, or what it raises on an exhausted or unknown opcode. Citation: genopStep cites `@3.14.7:2277-2295`, which is unchanged code now at :2305-2323.

name: genops
note: review: `return _genops(pickle)` (:2351); same entries as _genops and the same gap (an always-raising parse satisfies them). GenopsWellFormed also fixes hasTell = true, so the documented `pos is None` case without tell (:2345-2349) is stated nowhere.

name: optimize
note: review: optStep and optEmit mirror :2365-2417 (PUT/MEMOIZE/FRAME/GET/PROTO order, header at pos 0, newids renumbering, pickler.get(None), frameless large copies). But OptimizeRawCopy assumes no PUT, GET, MEMOIZE or FRAME and protocol < 4, which removes the function's whole purpose ('removing unused PUT opcodes', :2357) and the GET/PUT rewriting the brief names. That behaviour is the open pickle-optimize-sound. Probed true on 3.15.2: 19723 random raw-only streams copied exactly. Citations: OptSt/optStep `@3.14.7:2331-2359`/`:2337-2359` and OptOut/optEmit `@3.14.7:2371-2388`/`:2372-2388` are unchanged code, now at :2359-2387/:2365-2387 and :2399-2416/:2400-2416.

name: dis
note: review: The model mirrors the 3.15.2 body with the theme off: markPhase :2491-2519, memoPhase :2521-2540, argText :2542-2557, annotateLine with max(visible_len, annocol) :2558-2566, stackPhase :2574-2584, disEnd :2586-2592. The citations are correct. But DisFollowsGenops only constrains runs that raise nothing, and the refuted DisNoIndexError is one input, so a dis that raises IndexError on every stream satisfies both. None of the docstring's sanity checks (:2448-2459) is stated: the pop count, 'memo key never stored', 'can't store markobject', 'no MARK exists'. Neither are the rendered lines. Dropping any check passes. The refutation itself is true on 3.15.2: dis(b'(x85t.') gives IndexError('list index out of range'), and bugs/pickle-tools-dis-mark-indexerror.yaml exists.
